description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation by delivering (1) tenant-configurable retention controls across key data stores (audit logs, admin activity, inference request metadata, telemetry/analytics, and operational logs where applicable) and (2) a baseline “compliance reporting pack” that can be handed to enterprise prospects/customers and used internally for SOC 2/ISO-aligned evidence collection.

Goals:
- Product: Provide configurable retention policies per tenant (Hosted, Dedicated, and Private where feasible) with safe defaults, clear UI/UX in Console, and APIs for automation.
- Engineering: Implement enforceable retention in storage backends (deletion/compaction jobs, partition TTLs, export constraints), with provable behavior (tests + auditability).
- Compliance: Produce a standardized reporting pack including a control-to-evidence matrix, retention policy attestations, audit log coverage summary, and a repeatable evidence collection procedure.
- Customer readiness: Reduce friction in security reviews by making retention posture easy to explain and demonstrate.

Scope (in):
- Policy model: retention policy schema and evaluation (per data type, per tenant, per environment/region) with guardrails (min/max retention, legal hold override, “never delete” disallowed unless explicitly permitted).
- Enforcement: scheduled deletion/TTL enforcement for audit log storage and selected operational datasets; support for “legal hold” flags and exception workflow.
- Console: retention settings page, auditability (show effective policy, last enforcement run, exceptions/holds), and export-friendly views.
- Compliance pack: baseline documents (narrative + tables) and an internal runbook for generating and updating reports.

Scope (out / later):
- Full custom retention across every internal log stream (some infra logs remain governed by SRE standards and vendor limits).
- Customer-configurable retention for all raw inference payload content (depends on broader data handling choices and privacy posture).

Stakeholders:
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance) + Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts).
- Engineering: Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane), Chloe Martin/Jada Williams (Console), Logan Wright/Nadia Rahman (Telemetry), Marcus Lin/Kevin Osei (Security Eng).
- GRC/Compliance: Olga Petrov.
- Exec sponsor: Dr. Aisha Rahman.

Phases & timeline (typical 10–12 weeks):
1) Discovery & requirements (weeks 1–2): data inventory, customer requirements, policy guardrails, reporting pack outline.
2) Design (weeks 2–4): retention policy schema/ADR, enforcement approach per datastore, Console UX, evidence strategy.
3) Implementation (weeks 4–9): backend enforcement + migrations, Console settings, API endpoints, audit surfaces.
4) Reporting pack + validation (weeks 7–10): control mapping, internal evidence collection, customer-facing summaries.
5) Rollout (weeks 9–12): feature flag, staged rollout, monitoring, docs, support readiness.

Key deliverables:
- Retention policy engine + configuration surfaces (API + Console).
- Automated enforcement jobs with monitoring and auditability.
- Baseline compliance reporting pack (internal + customer-facing artifacts).
- Runbooks and support playbooks for exceptions/legal holds and customer questions.
